faq.question: How does Event Schedule pricing compare to Eventbrite?
faq.answer: Eventbrite's US pricing is a 3.7% + $1.79 service fee per paid ticket, plus a 2.9% payment processing fee per order. faq.question: Does Event Schedule have an event marketplace like Eventbrite?
faq.answer: Event Schedule focuses on giving organizers their own branded schedule pages rather than a shared marketplace. You get a dedicated URL (or your own domain on Enterprise), embeddable calendar widgets, a live calendar feed people can subscribe to, and an optional interest list on each event that emails people when tickets go on sale.

faq.question: Can I refund a ticket buyer?
faq.answer: Yes, from the Sales page. Refunds come with paid ticketing on Pro, because that is where the money is taken in the first place. A Stripe, PayPal or Razorpay sale can be refunded in full or in part, and the money goes back through the provider before the sale changes status. A partial refund keeps the tickets valid and shows how much has gone back so far; a full refund returns the tickets to sale. A sale paid another way, such as cash, is marked as refunded instead, because no money moves through us.

faq.question: Does Event Schedule do reserved seating?
faq.answer: Yes, on the Enterprise plan. A venue schedule draws its room once, with sections, rows, tables, standing areas and wheelchair spaces, and buyers pick their seats from the map at checkout. A box office view handles holds, phone bookings and seat moves. On Free and Pro, ticket types have a name, a price and a quantity, without assigned seats.

switch_steps.description: Connect Stripe or PayPal, or Razorpay for events priced in rupees, and tickets carry no booking fee. Paid tickets are on Pro.

switch_steps.title: Build an audience of your own
switch_steps.description: Show the follower QR code at your events. Whoever scans it can sign up to hear about your next ones from you, not from a city feed.

limits.title: Strangers will not stumble on you
limits.text: AllEvents says it reaches 20 million event seekers a month, in listings across more than 40,000 cities. The Event Schedule browse page shows one upcoming event per schedule, a far smaller window, so most of your audience will arrive through links you share.

limits.title: Nobody runs a campaign for you
limits.text: AllEvents sells promotion run by its own marketing team. The nearest thing here is boosting an event on Pro, a Facebook and Instagram ad that you set up and pay for yourself.

limits.title: Sends are counted per recipient
limits.text: On eventschedule.com a newsletter counts each recipient against a monthly allowance: 10 on Free, 100 on Pro and 1,000 on Enterprise. The limit lifts once the schedule sends through its own email settings, and the automatic digest of new events never counts against it.

faq.question: How does Event Schedule pricing compare to AllEvents?
faq.answer: AllEvents adds a booking fee of USD 1 to each paid ticket sold online (10% + INR 10 on events priced in rupees), charged to buyers unless you absorb it, and its paid plans at USD 12, 60 and 200 a month raise how many upcoming events you can list at once. Event Schedule has no booking fee, and Pro at $5/mo adds paid tickets with zero platform fees.

faq.question: Do I need a paid plan to list more events?
faq.answer: No. The free plan has no limit on events, and free registration with QR tickets is unlimited too. The AllEvents free plan allows 5 upcoming events at a time, and its paid plans raise that to 20, 100 or more.

faq.question: When do I get paid for ticket sales?
faq.answer: On Pro, paid tickets are charged through your own Stripe or PayPal account, so the money goes there as each order is placed. AllEvents also pays into your own PayPal or Stripe account, except for events priced in Indian rupees, which it pays out a few business days after the event.

faq.question: Can Event Schedule promote my event like AllEvents?
faq.answer: Event Schedule is built around your own schedule page rather than a shared marketplace. People who sign up on your schedule get an email when you add events, you can send newsletters, and on Pro you can boost an event with a Facebook and Instagram ad. If reaching strangers in your city matters most, AllEvents does more of that.

faq.question: Can I sell tickets on my own website?
faq.answer: Yes, on Pro. The ticket widget puts checkout on your own site, and the embeddable calendar, which is free, lists every upcoming event. AllEvents offers event list plugins and a ticket embed as well.

faq.question: Are the API and webhooks included?
faq.answer: Yes, both are on Pro at $5/mo, with a REST API for events, schedules and sales. AllEvents includes webhooks from its Essential plan at USD 12 a month, and its API is a data product for event listings rather than for managing your own events.

faq.question: Can people who do not know me still find my events?
faq.answer: Some can. Public events can appear on the Event Schedule browse page, which shows one upcoming event from each schedule, and every public event page can be listed by search engines. That is a much smaller audience than AllEvents' city listings.

faq.question: Can I sell tickets for an event priced in rupees?
faq.answer: Yes, on Pro, through Razorpay, which settles Indian rupees into your own Razorpay account with no platform fee from us. AllEvents charges buyers INR 10 a ticket on rupee events and takes 5% to 10% of sales from the organizer, and pays out a few business days after the event.

switch_steps.title: Bring the events in
switch_steps.description: Paste each Universe listing, as a link or as its text, into AI import, which fills in the event for you to check before it is saved.

switch_steps.title: Turn timeslots into dates
switch_steps.description: An event that repeated on Universe becomes one recurring event, daily or weekly on chosen days, with each date's tickets and capacity counted on their own.

switch_steps.title: Recreate questions and codes
switch_steps.description: Checkout questions become questions on a ticket type, free. Discount codes become promo codes, and the waitlist for sold-out tickets switches on, both on Pro.

switch_steps.title: Connect your own Stripe
switch_steps.description: If you connected your own Stripe account to Universe, connect it here as well, or use PayPal. Selling a priced ticket is on Pro, and no service fee is added.

limits.title: Dates, not half-hour slots
limits.text: Universe's timed-entry tools give an attraction many entry times a day, each with its own price and capacity. A recurring event here repeats by date at one start time, so it suits a weekly class or a nightly show better than an attraction that admits a group every half hour.

limits.title: Tickets sell where you put them
limits.text: Universe's custom Pro plans can list your tickets on Ticketmaster. Event Schedule has no distribution partner: tickets sell on your schedule and event pages, and on Pro in the ticket widget on your own website.

limits.title: The mailing list lives here
limits.text: Universe can sync attendees to Mailchimp, and Event Schedule does not connect to Mailchimp at all. Buyers who tick the box at checkout join your email subscribers, and newsletters to them are written and sent from inside the app.

faq.question: How does Event Schedule pricing compare to Universe?
faq.answer: Universe charges US organizers 2% + $0.79 per paid ticket on its Starter plan, plus a 3% processing fee through Universe Payments, passed on to buyers or absorbed by you. Event Schedule Pro is a flat $5/mo with zero platform fees, so you pay only Stripe's or PayPal's own processing.

faq.question: When do I get paid?
faq.answer: On Pro, paid tickets are charged through your own Stripe or PayPal account, so the money goes there as each order is placed. With Universe Payments, funds reach your Universe balance 48 hours after the event ends, and connecting your own Stripe account is its option for money before the event.

faq.question: Does Event Schedule have reserved seating?
faq.answer: Yes, on Enterprise. A venue schedule draws its room once, with sections, rows, tables, standing areas and wheelchair spaces, and buyers pick their seats from the map at checkout. Universe stopped offering seating plans for new listings in 2019.

faq.question: Can I run a long series of dates?
faq.answer: Yes. Recurring events repeat daily, weekly on chosen days, every few weeks or monthly, with dates you can skip, and each date keeps its own tickets and capacity. For attractions with many entry times a day, Universe's timed-entry events go further.

faq.question: Can I keep my events in Google Calendar?
faq.answer: Yes. Google Calendar sync runs both ways on every plan, and Outlook and CalDAV calendars sync the same way. Anyone can also subscribe to your schedule's live calendar feed.

faq.question: Is it easy to switch from Universe?
faq.answer: Yes. Create a free schedule, paste your event details or upload a flyer and the AI parser fills in each event for you to check, then connect Stripe or PayPal and move to Pro to sell paid tickets.

faq.question: Does Event Schedule have a door app like BoxOffice?
faq.answer: There is nothing to install: tickets are scanned in the browser on any phone, free on every plan, and each ticket admits once. Pro adds a live count of arrivals, broken down by ticket type. Taking a card payment in person is not something Event Schedule does.

faq.question: Can I keep some tickets for invited guests only?
faq.answer: Not with a password on one ticket type, as Universe allows. On Enterprise a whole event can be Unlisted, reachable only by its link and optionally behind a password, and on Pro a promo code gives the people you choose a lower price.
